name: Reid Hoffman

summary.text: Reid Hoffman is an entrepreneur and investor who co-founded LinkedIn in 2003, was a founding board member and executive vice president of PayPal, and has been a partner at Greylock since 2009. He invested in Facebook's first outside funding round in 2004, which Peter Thiel led; Hoffman has said he declined to lead it himself and suggested Thiel do so.

sources.title: Reid Hoffman (partner biography)
Reid Hoffman interview (on the 2004 Facebook round)
Reid Hoffman Invested $37,500 Into Facebook At A $5M Valuation

facts.claim: Hoffman was a founding board member of PayPal and later served as its executive vice president, responsible for the company's external relationships.

sources.title: Reid Hoffman (partner biography)

facts.claim: In 2004, Sean Parker contacted Hoffman about investing in Facebook. Hoffman has said he chose not to lead the round because of how his roles at LinkedIn and Friendster might look, suggested that Peter Thiel lead it instead, and invested himself. TechCrunch reported his stake as $37,500.

sources.title: Reid Hoffman interview (on the 2004 Facebook round)
Reid Hoffman Invested $37,500 Into Facebook At A $5M Valuation

facts.claim: Hoffman received a B.S. in Symbolic Systems from Stanford University in 1990 and an M.S. in Philosophy from Oxford University in 1993, according to PayPal's annual report.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: Hoffman studied philosophy at Oxford as a Marshall Scholar (class of 1990).

sources.title: Reid Hoffman profile

facts.claim: Hoffman worked in human interface design at Apple Computer, in the group that built the eWorld online service, before leaving in early 1996.
facts.quote: the group I was working in was called the eWorld group.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001
Reid Hoffman (interview)

facts.claim: Hoffman worked in product development for Fujitsu from February 1996 to July 1997.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: Hoffman said his first company, first named Relationships.com and later renamed SocialNet, was financed in November 1997; he called it a failure and said its investors got their capital back.
facts.quote: We did return our capital to our investors, but we didn't actually make an ongoing company.

sources.title: Reid Hoffman (interview)

facts.claim: Hoffman served as a director of Confinity, Inc. (PayPal's predecessor) from December 1998 to January 2000, the same month Confinity was co-founded.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: Hoffman joined PayPal full-time in January 2000, held posts including Senior Vice President of Business Development and International, and became Executive Vice President of Business Development in May 2000. He has said his first PayPal title was COO.
facts.quote: I think my first title at PayPal was COO.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001
Reid Hoffman (interview)

facts.claim: In July 2001 PayPal lent Hoffman $500,000 under a non-recourse employee 'liquidity program' at 5.02% interest; in September 2001 the company bought back part of participants' shares at $3 per share, and the proceeds repaid the loans.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: LinkedIn was incorporated in Delaware in March 2003 as LinkedIn, Ltd. Hoffman, a co-founder, served on its board from March 2003, as CEO from March 2003 to February 2007 and again from December 2008 to June 2009, and became board chair in December 2010.

sources.title: LinkedIn Corporation prospectus (Form 424B4), initial public offering

facts.claim: Before LinkedIn's May 2011 IPO (priced at $45 per Class A share), a living trust of which Hoffman is a co-trustee held 19,066,032 Class B shares (21.2%); it offered 115,335 shares in the IPO. Sequoia-affiliated entities held 18.7% and Greylock-affiliated entities 15.6%. LinkedIn said Hoffman's Class B shares (10 votes each) would carry about 21.7% of voting power after the offering.

sources.title: LinkedIn Corporation prospectus (Form 424B4), initial public offering

facts.claim: Hoffman has been a partner at Greylock Partners since November 2009, according to LinkedIn's IPO prospectus. Greylock had been a LinkedIn investor before then; Greylock partner David Sze had sat on LinkedIn's board since September 2004.

sources.title: LinkedIn Corporation prospectus (Form 424B4), initial public offering

facts.claim: On June 13, 2016, Microsoft agreed to buy LinkedIn for $196 per share in cash, a deal valued at $26.2 billion including LinkedIn's net cash, financed mainly by new debt. Microsoft's release called Hoffman LinkedIn's 'controlling shareholder' and quoted his support for the deal.
facts.quote: I fully support this transaction and the Board's decision to pursue it.

sources.title: Microsoft Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.2: Microsoft to acquire LinkedIn (press release)

facts.claim: As of the July 18, 2016 record date, Hoffman beneficially owned 14,489,899 LinkedIn shares, about 11% of the stock and about 53% of the voting power, enough to approve the merger alone. At $196 per share that stake works out to about $2.84 billion before taxes (a calculation from the filing's figures, not a number the filing gives).

sources.title: LinkedIn Corporation definitive merger proxy statement (DEFM14A)

facts.claim: The merger proxy says Hoffman initially preferred a cash-and-stock deal structured as a tax-free reorganization. He declined to sign a support agreement with Microsoft because it could have triggered automatic conversion of his Class B shares, then backed an all-cash offer as part of a higher price.

sources.title: LinkedIn Corporation definitive merger proxy statement (DEFM14A)

facts.claim: Microsoft's board appointed Hoffman a director on March 14, 2017, assigning him to its Regulatory and Public Policy Committee. On June 2, 2026 he told Microsoft he would not stand for re-election at the 2026 annual meeting; Microsoft said this was not due to any disagreement with management.

sources.title: Microsoft Form 8-K: appointment of Reid Hoffman to the Board
Microsoft Form 8-K: Reid Hoffman not standing for re-election

facts.claim: Hoffman wrote that Greylock led Airbnb's Series A in November 2010 after a divided partner meeting, with him bringing the deal to the firm.
facts.quote: Greylock led Airbnb's Series A in November 2010.

sources.title: Airbnb reflections (by Reid Hoffman)

facts.claim: Inflection AI was announced in March 2022, co-founded by Hoffman, DeepMind co-founder Mustafa Suleyman (CEO) and Karén Simonyan (chief scientist).

sources.title: Deepmind and LinkedIn founders promise new interface era

facts.claim: In June 2023 Inflection raised $1.3 billion in a round led by Microsoft and Nvidia, with Hoffman, Bill Gates and Eric Schmidt investing personally; Forbes reported a $4 billion valuation, citing a source.

sources.title: Inflection AI, the year-old startup behind chatbot Pi, raises US$1.3 billion

facts.claim: In March 2024 Microsoft took a non-exclusive license to Inflection's intellectual property. Microsoft's proxy disclosed that Hoffman co-founded Inflection and sits on its board, that Greylock-affiliated entities and Reprogrammed Interchange LLC each held under 10% of Inflection, that Hoffman may be deemed to own those shares beneficially, and that he did not take part in the board's review and approval of the deal.

sources.title: Microsoft 2024 proxy statement (DEF 14A), related-party transactions section

facts.claim: Microsoft hired Suleyman, Simonyan and most of Inflection's staff and paid Inflection a license fee reported at about $650 million (figure from The Information). The UK CMA opened a merger inquiry on 16 July 2024. On 4 September 2024 it cleared the deal at Phase 1, finding that it counted as a merger but did not raise competition concerns.

sources.title: Microsoft / Inflection inquiry (case page)
UK regulator greenlights Microsoft's Inflection acquihire, but also designates it a merger

facts.claim: CNN reported in July 2024 that the FTC had launched an investigation into Microsoft's recent deal with AI startup Inflection, which Hoffman co-founded, while Hoffman sat on Microsoft's board.

sources.title: LinkedIn billionaire is going all in on Kamala Harris. But he wants her to make a big change

facts.claim: Hoffman announced in March 2023 that he was leaving OpenAI's board, citing the appearance of a conflict from his involvement with a competing AI company. Semafor later reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that he was privately unhappy at being asked to leave by Sam Altman.

sources.title: Reid Hoffman was privately unhappy about leaving OpenAI's board

facts.claim: In July 2024 Hoffman, who had given $7 million to the pro-Biden and Harris super PAC Future Forward according to CNN, told CNN that FTC Chair Lina Khan was 'not helping America.' He said he would hope Vice President Harris 'would replace her.' He said he had certainly not directly pushed Harris to do so. A Harris campaign aide said there had been no policy discussions about replacing Khan.

sources.title: LinkedIn billionaire is going all in on Kamala Harris. But he wants her to make a big change

facts.claim: A Washington Examiner analysis of FEC filings found Hoffman had given at least $11.6 million to help elect Harris as of October 2024: $6 million to Future Forward in March 2024 (his largest political gift since 2002, per the analysis), $4 million more to the PAC in April and June, and money to American Bridge and the Republican Accountability PAC.

sources.title: Meet Kamala Harris's influential megadonors

facts.claim: FEC records reported in July 2026 show Hoffman gave $10 million to Lone Star Rising, the main super PAC backing Democratic Texas Senate nominee James Talarico, nearly 80% of its second-quarter receipts. The Texas Tribune put his total giving to candidates and committees since 2016 at roughly $77 million.

sources.title: Billionaire Reid Hoffman gives $10 million to super PAC backing Talarico's Senate bid in Texas

facts.claim: In December 2018 Hoffman apologized after reports that $750,000 he gave to American Engagement Technologies (AET) went partly to a project in the 2017 Alabama Senate race that used fake social-media accounts against Roy Moore. He said he had not known of the tactics and rejected the use of misinformation.
facts.quote: I categorically disavow the use of misinformation to sway an election

sources.title: LinkedIn Co-Founder Apologizes for Funding Misinformation Campaign Against Roy Moore

facts.claim: Hoffman's nonprofit, American Future Republic, helped fund some of E. Jean Carroll's expenses in her civil suits against Donald Trump. In May 2026 CNN reported, citing sources, the following. Federal prosecutors in Chicago were examining whether Carroll made false statements about how her case was funded, and the probe was also scrutinizing the nonprofit. The U.S. attorney said no criminal investigation into Carroll had been opened. Hoffman said the probe is meant to 'silence' those who stand up to Trump. He said he had never taken any steps to hide his financial support for the lawsuit.

sources.title: Reid Hoffman says E. Jean Carroll probe involving his nonprofit is meant to 'silence' Trump critics

facts.claim: In 2019 Hoffman told Axios his interactions with Jeffrey Epstein were for MIT Media Lab fundraising at Joi Ito's request, and that Ito had told him Epstein had cleared MIT's vetting. He apologized, saying that by taking part he helped repair Epstein's reputation.
facts.quote: I helped to repair his reputation and perpetuate injustice. For this, I am deeply regretful.

sources.title: Newly released emails and a Trump-ordered investigation thrust Reid Hoffman into the Epstein firestorm

facts.claim: Records add detail to Hoffman's account. MIT's external report says Ito sought his advice in July 2016 on Epstein attending a Media Lab event. A March 2017 Epstein email to Hoffman proposed a donor-advised fund, and the released emails do not show whether he replied. The WSJ reported that Hoffman visited Epstein's island in 2014 for a fundraising trip Ito requested. It also reported that he offered to help Epstein with bad publicity after sex-trafficking allegations surfaced in late 2014. Hoffman says he was never Epstein's client and dealt with him only for MIT fundraising. He has said he 'very much' regrets that relationship.

sources.title: Newly released emails and a Trump-ordered investigation thrust Reid Hoffman into the Epstein firestorm

sources.publisher: The Wall Street Journal (via To Vima)
sources.title: The Famous Names in the Latest Release of Epstein Files

facts.claim: On February 3, 2026, Hoffman said on X that his 2019 statement that his last contact with Epstein was in 2015 was inaccurate. He said a review of his calendar showed at least six meetings after 2015, some in person and some by call. At least five were between April and July 2016, and the last was on March 24, 2018. He said all were tied to MIT Media Lab fundraising coordinated by Joi Ito, and that he had no personal relationship with Epstein. He said: 'I only knew Jeffrey Epstein because of a fundraising relationship with MIT, which I very much regret.' He added that Epstein's victims deserve all the information they are seeking.

sources.title: 'I very much regret it': Reid Hoffman admits to meeting Jeffrey Epstein multiple times after 2015

sources.publisher: The Wall Street Journal (via To Vima)
sources.title: The Famous Names in the Latest Release of Epstein Files

facts.claim: In November 2025 President Trump posted that the Justice Department was 'looking at' Democrats including Hoffman over Epstein ties. Attorney General Pam Bondi said on November 13 that she would start an investigation. Hoffman called it 'political persecution and slander' and urged Trump to release all of the Epstein files.

sources.title: Newly released emails and a Trump-ordered investigation thrust Reid Hoffman into the Epstein firestorm

facts.claim: NBC News reported in February 2026 that Hoffman said on X that he 'only knew Jeffrey Epstein because of a fundraising relationship' with MIT, 'which I very much regret,' and that he went to Epstein's island 'with Joi Ito, the Director of the MIT Media Lab, who had asked me to help MIT fundraise from Epstein.'
facts.quote: Hoffman said on X that he "only knew Jeffrey Epstein because of a fundraising relationship" with MIT, "which I very much regret." He also said he went to Epstein's island "with Joi Ito, the Director of the MIT Media Lab, who had asked me to help MIT fundraise from Epstein."

sources.title: Latest Epstein files release rattles Silicon Valley

facts.claim: The Justice Department's 2026 release includes a July 2013 message in which Epstein asked Joi Ito about the jail; Ito replied that he had talked to Hoffman about it and that Hoffman 'doesn't judge people.' NBC News reported that there is no indication in the documents that Hoffman knew of Epstein's alleged ongoing crimes during their acquaintance.
facts.quote: In a July 2013 message to Joi Ito, then director of MIT's Media Lab, Epstein asked about the jail; Ito replied that he had talked to Hoffman about it and that he doesn't judge people.

sources.title: Latest Epstein files release rattles Silicon Valley

facts.claim: In February 2026 Hoffman posted on X, over a news headline about the Justice Department's release: 'Fixed your headline: LinkedIn founder Reid Hoffman exonerated by Trump's FBI in newly released Epstein DOJ docs. Release all the files. Prosecute the abusers.' The 'exonerated' characterization is Hoffman's; no official finding to that effect has been reported.
facts.quote: Fixed your headline: LinkedIn founder Reid Hoffman exonerated by Trump's FBI in newly released Epstein DOJ docs. Release all the files. Prosecute the abusers.

sources.title: Fixed your headline: LinkedIn founder Reid Hoffman exonerated by Trump's FBI in newly released Epstein DOJ docs

facts.claim: The Wall Street Journal reported in August 2023, from Epstein's emails and schedules, that Hoffman introduced Peter Thiel to Epstein and that Epstein then scheduled at least six meetings with Thiel at his townhouse from 2014 to 2016. Hoffman said he made the introduction to fundraise for MIT and regretted the association: 'I trusted MIT's vetting and did not do my own.'
facts.quote: Hoffman later said he regretted the association and that he had introduced Thiel in order to fundraise for MIT. "I trusted MIT's vetting and did not do my own," Hoffman said.

sources.publisher: Daily Caller (reporting a Wall Street Journal story)
sources.title: Democrat Megadonor Reportedly Introduced Trump Backer To Jeffrey Epstein

facts.quote: on July 19, 2013, Epstein visited the MIT campus and met with then–Media Lab director Joi Ito and Reid Hoffman.

facts.claim: Press reports in December 2018 said Hoffman's $750,000 went to American Engagement Technologies (AET), a company founded in October 2017 and run by Mikey Dickerson, the founding director of the United States Digital Service, and that AET passed money to the research firm New Knowledge for the Alabama project known as 'Project Birmingham', whose reported budget was $100,000. Hoffman's statement to the Washington Post was the first time he acknowledged financial ties to AET.
facts.quote: Hoffman's investment was passed through a company called American Engagement Technologies (AET), which was run by Mikey Dickerson, the founding director of the United States Digital Service

sources.title: LinkedIn cofounder apologizes for funding election disinformation campaign in Alabama

facts.claim: In a Medium post titled 'Truth and Politics' and a statement to the Washington Post on December 26, 2018, Hoffman said he had never heard of the Alabama project before reading the New York Times' coverage, had never personally authorized or directed any funding to New Knowledge, did not know why AET supported it, was embarrassed by his failure to track AET more diligently, and supported a federal investigation.
facts.quote: he had never even heard of this project before reading about it in the Times' coverage

facts.claim: A complaint filed with the Federal Election Commission (Matter Under Review 7562) asserted that money for the 2017 Alabama disinformation effort flowed through American Engagement Technologies, the firm Hoffman funded. The FEC's closed-matters listing shows MUR 7562, case name New Knowledge, closed with a disposition of 'Dismissed-Other' for three respondents, on subjects of prohibited and corporate contributions.
facts.quote: money flowed through American Engagement Technologies, a firm run by Mikey Dickerson

facts.claim: After his July 2024 CNN remarks on Lina Khan, Hoffman posted on X that he had never spoken with Vice President Harris about Khan or about the FTC generally, and had never demanded that Harris fire Khan if elected; he told CNN's Jake Tapper his view was offered as an 'expert', not as a donor. Senator Bernie Sanders responded that billionaires should not be telling candidates whom to keep on. Searches for 2025 and 2026 statements by Hoffman on Khan or the FTC found none.
facts.quote: he had never spoken with Vice President Harris about Lina Khan, or even about the FTC generally

openQuestions: Who financed SocialNet in 1997-1999? CB Insights (an aggregator; not opened in full) lists Accel, PRIMEDIA, Talk City, Tribune Ventures and St. Paul Venture Capital and about $23.8M over five rounds; no press release or filing confirming this was found.
Whether Hoffman invested his own money in Confinity when he joined its board in December 1998: no filing or interview found saying so.
Details of the Hoffman-Thiel Stanford student government run (year, office) reported by The New Republic were not confirmed in a primary source.
No public record found of Hoffman holding finance-industry, government or intelligence roles before 1999; the 10-K bio lists only Apple, Fujitsu and Socialnet.com.
Hoffman's actual cash proceeds from the 2016 LinkedIn sale (after any earlier sales, trusts or donations) and the Microsoft shares or options he received as a director: not found in filings opened.
Final FEC totals for Hoffman's 2024 giving (the FEC API was rate-limited in this session). Figures used come from a pre-election Washington Examiner analysis and from CNN.

'Investing in US', the political investment vehicle reportedly set up by Hoffman and Dmitri Mehlhorn after 2016, and its grantees (Indivisible, AET and others): only partisan or secondary sources found, none opened.
CNBC (Nov 2023) reportedly cited FEC data showing over $1.5 million from Hoffman to Mainstream Democrats PAC; the page returned 403.
The reported $7 million American Future Republic paid toward Carroll's legal costs (said to come from 2023 tax filings): not verified from the filing.
The date Hoffman joined OpenAI's board, and the amount of his early OpenAI donation (2015 launch pledge): the OpenAI page returned 403.
The current status of the FTC inquiry into Microsoft–Inflection: no closing record found.
When Hoffman joined Airbnb's board and whether he is still on it: his O'Reilly bio lists a seat but gives no date.
Ties to David Sacks: no record found of co-investments or shared boards; one data-aggregator page listing Hoffman as a Yammer board member looks unreliable.
The venue of the August 2015 dinner (Baumé restaurant vs. Hoffman's home): reports differ.

The Christmas Eve 2014 Hoffman-to-Epstein email ('ice cream ... for the girls') and the representative's explanation that 'the girls' were adult staff were found only on advocacy or aggregator sites and were left out.
Hoffman's X post about the island visit is cited through NBC News; the post itself and its date were not located.
The Wall Street Journal's 2023 story is cited through the Daily Caller's account; verify against the Journal.
The Medium post 'Truth and Politics' and the Washington Post statement were not opened directly; quotes are as reported by TechCrunch, Fast Company and the Daily Beast.
MUR 7562's respondents and closing date were not seen; whether Hoffman or AET were respondents is unconfirmed. Check fec.gov/data/legal/matter-under-review/7562.
No 2025 or 2026 statement by Hoffman on Lina Khan or the FTC under Chairman Ferguson surfaced in searches; the file's Khan material remains from July to September 2024.
